_comment: Upstream digests for the committed .fabro fork. Regenerate with `just refresh-fork-upstream-pins`; every entry MUST carry a reason. The workflow.toml digest normalizes only the upstream docker pin value. See crates/console-fork-drift-check/src/lib.rs.

files.reason: ABSENT FROM OUR FORK BY CONSTRUCTION. Upstream added a whole `disposition` stage; our workflow.fabro has zero references to it. Adopting it is a graph change, not a file copy. `present_in_fork: false` records that this omission is known, so the gate does not report it as a missing file every run.
DIVERGED only slightly from upstream. Low-risk to sync; not yet reviewed.

DIVERGED. Upstream has grown honest-checks / no-detector-evasion, cohesion-decomposition and verbatim-move rules we have not adopted. Porting them is wanted but is its own reviewed change, not a silent sync.

SYNCED VERBATIM from upstream 2026-07-28 (PR #476, merged 2026-07-28T22:08:32Z) — our copy had been frozen at 3fa2d5c and lacked the fetch+rebase publish leg that upstream landed as bd-ib-qq7f (PR #905). Keep it verbatim: a local 'improvement' to borrowed prose becomes a divergence nobody remembers agreeing to. The retry's exact-match ci.yml scoping is a known upstream wart, filed with factory-hardening; we inherit the fix when they ship it.

DELIBERATELY NOT SYNCED, same reason as review.md — and upstream has additionally rewritten it to consume a `disposition` record that our graph does not produce, so syncing it alone would reference a stage we do not run.

DELIBERATELY NOT SYNCED. This repo's review gate is ADVISORY / ship-on-cap by recorded decision (workflow.fabro, work-item bd-ib-egms32); upstream's is BLOCKING by default. Syncing would silently revert a ratified policy. Re-pin on upstream change only after confirming the change is policy-neutral.

DIVERGED. Our graph encodes the advisory ship-on-cap review gate (see :9-10, bd-ib-egms32) and omits upstream's disposition stage. This is the file the fork exists to own; treat any upstream movement here as a design review, never a sync.

DIVERGED: this Rust console fork deliberately pins the Rust-capable `python-rust-agent-` sandbox image, while upstream pins the Python-only `python-agent-` image. The fork-drift gate normalizes exactly that upstream docker value before hashing workflow.toml, so upstream docker tag bumps no longer require re-review; every other upstream byte in workflow.toml remains pinned and must still be reviewed or ported
